主要内容: Amazon (AMZN) reported Q1 2020 earnings with a $3.1 billion operating income, up from the same quarter last year. The company saw a surge in grocery sales, with physical store sales rising 8% year-over-year, mainly in March. Olsavsky attributed shipping delays to inventory shortages, not logistics issues. Amazon also announced a $10 billion coronavirus response plan, including 100 million face masks and higher pay for hourly workers. It suspended over 10,000 sellers for price gouging and expanded food delivery. AWS revenue reached $10.22 billion, surpassing $10 billion for the first time. Amazon expects Q2 net sales between $75 billion and $81 billion, with year-over-year growth between 18% and 28%. The company anticipates an operating loss of $1.5 billion to an operating income of $1.5 billion due to pandemic-related spending. AWS supported the NFL's virtual draft and global coronavirus response efforts, including the World Health Organization and schools.
